Hetor was by far the youngest Voidborn aboard the *Eldest*. At less than a million years old, he was one of the youngest Trainees in the Alliance. Most of the older Voidborn simply ignored him when he was shadowing them at their work, so he was surprised when Ghoti turned to him during his inspection of the biolabs and spoke.

*What is your evaluation of this scenario?*

*Err...* Hetor didn't know if Ghoti honestly wanted his opinion or if this was a test. He decided to treat it like an assessment. *The gods of this system have erected barriers sufficient to keep us out of the planet for now. This means that we have no ability to observe their actions and limited punishment capability. Without deterrence, they will be inflicting countless atrocities on-*

*You are reciting.*

Hetor stopped, abashed.

*Showing off has a purpose. We used it to great effect when we arrived here. But this is not the time to be ostentatious. Now is the time for subtelty.*

Ghoti softly recited the mantra of the Voidborn Watch.

*First, they ignore us.*

*Then, they laugh at us.*

*Then, they fight us.*

*Then, we win.*

He paused, and looked down at Hetor for a long moment. Then he spoke.

*Why is it that you think these gods took the step of blocking all technology within Solus, exiling one of their own.*

Hetor replied hesistantly *Well, to keep us out of course...*

*And what does it imply that they wanted to keep us out so badly?*

*Well... that they felt they had to?*

*Very good. The gods are afraid. Our show of force demonstrated our ability to hurt them, and hide from them, and so they have hidden from us. They fear us. That is good, fear is the first step to subjugation.*

Ghoti gestured at the horrific creature taking shape in the lab's containment area.

*Godly memory is highly volatile. They invent histories and pasts for themselves, even rewrite their own memories to maintain their self-images. We have made ourselves objects of fear to them, but they have never truly seen us. Right now they will be in a frenzy of creation behind their walls, trying to create a world in their image before they are no more. This is normal. And we will wait, silently, never publicly announcing our presence, but giving subtle reminders. In this time, the gods will rewrite us in their memories, imagining us as their worst nightmares. They will feed on each other's fear and grow more afraid. And we shall seed on the outer surface of Solus horrors designed by memetics to embody the worst fears of the gods, all the while cloaking ourselves. In time they will conflate us with our creations, grow confident again.*

*And then...?*

*And then we crush them. Greater depths of fear are achieved by a rise and fall than by overwhelming force alone. We shall have yet another system of tame gods, obeying our will. Such is the way of things, as they are and as they always will be. Existence is solely to serve the Void. Mortals can be Purged, gods cannot. And so we teach the gods to serve us by the power of fear.*

*I see.*

Ghoti fell silent, and Hetor couldn't shake the feeling that he had failed some sort of test.
